decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0.75% to 1%. The vote was 9-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen even as growth in economic activity slowed.

changes.quote: Job gains were solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate declined.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains remained solid and the unemployment rate was little changed in recent months.”

changes.quote: Household spending rose only modestly, but the fundamentals underpinning the continued growth of consumption remained solid.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Inflation measured on a 12-month basis recently has been running close to the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective.

changes.quote: Excluding energy and food, consumer prices declined in March and inflation continued to run somewhat below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.
Excluding energy and food, consumer prices declined in March and inflation continued to run somewhat below 2 percent.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.41% APR costs about $51.71 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.33% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.97% would rise by about $6.91 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of 187k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.4% over the past year (March 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.13%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.01% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 94%, cut 0%, hike 6%.

citations.detail: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3/4 to 1 percent.
